news.title: Visa Brings USDC Prefunding to Commercial Payouts
news.body: Visa moved stablecoin-enabled prefunding into commercial deployment through Inyo Global, letting eligible businesses fund Visa Direct cross-border payouts with USDC through existing APIs while recipients receive fiat. The service adds a funding option without requiring recipients to adopt crypto wallets. Available corridors, conversion costs and required balances will determine how it compares with existing funding arrangements; the announcement does not demonstrate liquidity savings.

news.title: Upgrade Seeks Nevada Bank Charter Alongside Existing Partnerships
news.body: After facilitating more than $53 billion in credit through its bank-and-loan-buyer model, Upgrade applied to establish a Nevada industrial loan bank. The company says an owned bank would complement those relationships rather than replace partners. Approval would give Upgrade an additional funding and origination option, but the application does not establish an approval timetable or the eventual division of business between its bank and external partners.

news.title: Equifax Adds Mastercard Cash-Flow Data to Lenders’ Credit Assessment Tools
news.body: Lenders using Equifax will gain access to Mastercard Open Finance insights alongside consumer credit files, including cash-flow analytics covering up to 24 months of credits, debits and balances. The tools support assessments of thin-file and credit-invisible consumers within existing underwriting systems. Mastercard gains distribution through Equifax, which retains a multi-provider approach; the announcement provides no quantified improvement in approvals or default outcomes.

news.title: Intuit Targets Usage-Based Billing With Sequence Acquisition
news.body: Intuit announced plans to acquire Sequence for undisclosed terms, adding pricing, billing, collection and revenue-management capabilities for usage-, consumption-, seat- and milestone-based business models. The proposed deal targets B2B software and professional-services businesses within Intuit’s mid-market offering. It would bring more of their contract-to-collection workflow into one platform, although the acquisition announcement does not make those capabilities immediately available.

news.title: Scams and Stolen Credentials Account for Half of Surveyed Fraud Dollars
news.body: Scams represented 22.4% of reported fraud dollars and account takeover through stolen credentials represented 28.2% in a July 2026 survey of 90 executives at U.S. banks, credit unions and fintechs. Together, the categories accounted for 50.6%. Separately, 78% of respondents cited new-system complexity as their leading innovation barrier. These findings describe the surveyed institutions, not a census of national fraud losses, and do not establish which interventions reduce losses.

perspective: Visa expands payout funding as Upgrade seeks a bank charter, alongside cash-flow underwriting, billing consolidation and fraud-loss survey findings.

curiosity.text: Western Union introduced its money-transfer service in 1871. Telegraphic transfers communicated payment instructions over the telegraph network rather than physically transporting the sender’s cash to the recipient—a distinction between moving information and moving money. Historical source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, https://www.britannica.com/money/Western-Union-Corporation
